  Mayor's Fund Subcommittee
  • Chair Jim Howat provided an overview of the last subcommittee meeting,
  they discussed the Standard Operating Procedures, the members would like
  to continue to work on the SOP before a final vote from the committee.
  • The subcommittee is also exploring new funding initiatives for the Mayor’s
  Fund and is collaborating with staff to develop and present fresh ideas.
  Policy Subcommittee
  • Chair Sarah Bedy provided updates on the 2024 Homeless Services
  Advisory Committee Annual Report with Policy Recommendations. The
  subcommittee is looking to bring in a speaker to talk about state
  legislation propositions.
  Long Beach CoC Updates
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an overview on the last Long Beach
  CoC board meeting, the board received a presentation of the federal funding
  impacts, the board will be having their annual retreat in September.
  • The board elected two new co-chairs during the last meeting, Tamika Boyce
  and Claude Diles.

3.  25-55407  Recommendation to approve the 2024 Homeless Services Advisory Committee
  Annual Report with Policy Recommendations.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Hilliard, Scott, Wood, Lie

  • Committee member Sarah Bedy presented the Annual Report with policy
  recommendations to the committee, including edits made by Chair Julie Lie.
  The committee engaged in discussion about the report, during which
  member Leanna shared insights from the recent annual budget meeting she

  attended on Tuesday. She emphasized the importance of the committee
  focusing on upstream solutions.
  • Staff and committee members also discussed recent encampment activity
  and the need for the committee to take a more proactive approach. Following
  the discussion, the committee moved to approve the policy
  recommendations.

4.  25-55962  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on the Homeless Services
  Bureau Outreach team approaches from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Chotiswatdi, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Hilliard, Scott, Wood, Lie

  • City staff Joel Reynoza provided an overview presentation on the Homeless
  Services Bureau Outreach staff approaches. The team works at the pace of
  each participant but the priority is housing. Consistency is a crucial factor
  when engaging with individuals, as it helps build trust between staff and
  those they serve.
  • Field staff are able to provide resources such as referrals to shelter and
  specialist, housing queue referrals, transportation, notary public, connection
  to job services, treatment, mental health, medical connection and move-in
  support.
  • Staff and committee members discussed that the MSC location is not ideal;
  however, people still find ways to access the MSC despite its less-than-ideal
  location.
  • A member of the public questioned the after hours approach that civilians
  should use when they see a homeless person after calling PD does this get
  referred over to HSB.

5.  25-55321  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Quarterly
  Operations Data Report and Staff Operations and Updates Report from the Health
  Department.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Hilliard, Scott, Wood, Lie

  • Staff member Dalton Dorr presented the quarterly data report, which was
  compiled during the HMIS merger. The committee members would like to
  receive more detailed information regarding some of the data presented.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided the operations and staff report., the
  department of health and Human Services is going through a loss of multiple
  funding sources/grants.
  • Long Beach is seeing a reduction in LAHSA’s interim housing, beds that are
  funded at Atlantic Bridge Community.
  • The Long Beach Youth Navigation center ribbon cutting was 8/6/25, the 12
  youth shelter beds will open in late August early September.
  • The Luxury Inn is nearing completion, the ribbon cutting will be early
  September with occupancy by late September.
  • HSB will be working closely with the housing authority to support with
  transitioning the approximately 530 households currently utilizing EHVs.
  • Skybridge Housing Development and home have received funding from
  DMH for 150 beds and Roots and Recovery transitional Living Homes have
  recovery bridge funding.
  • City Staff responded to the Tsunami warnings by conducting outreach to
  individuals in the riverbed.

6.  25-55323  Recommendation to receive and file the future Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee (HSAC) agenda items.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Hilliard, Scott, Wood, Lie

  • Member Pam expressed interest in receiving more updates on
  youth programs and available resources.
